At midnight, the pen rolled off Lina’s desk by itself and tapped three times against the floor, as if asking to be picked up. When she pressed it to the paper, it did not write her thoughts but a warning in a shaky blue hand: Do not let the sunrise read this. Heart hammering, Lina kept writing anyway, and each sentence revealed another piece of a story she had no memory of living—a train of glass, a city underwater, a brother she had lost twice. By dawn, the final line appeared: When you reach the last word, look out the window. She did, and there on the empty street stood her brother, dripping seawater and smiling like he had just walked out of a dream.
